描述_ZN: The Sounding Horses" scroll, modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 102.5 cm in length and 35.7 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "Lamenting and thinking of battle, standing very tall to the pale. Written by Beihong at the China Academy of Art in Panxi in the spring of the year Cuxu." Inscription: "Xu" in vermilion.　　The year of Cuxu was 1946, and Xu Beihong was 51 years old.　　The picture depicts a horse with a flying mane, looking into the distance and whistling in the wilderness. The poem "Wailing and thinking of battle, standing very tall to the pale" is a poem by Du Fu of the Tang Dynasty, and it is also Xu Beihong's favorite inscription on the picture of a horse, expressing a spirit of resistance that is not willing to yield in the face of difficulties.  Panxi is located in Sichuan Province between the mountains and forests on the north bank of the Jialing River, named Panxi because of a clear spring running out of the rocky mountainside into a clear stream. From 1943, Xu Beihong started to use the ancestral hall here to organize a research institution, the China Academy of Fine Arts, which employed Zhang Daqian, Wu Zuoren, Chen Xiaonan, Li Ruinian, Zhang Anzhi, Zhang Yingqian and others as researchers. This picture was painted before he was about to leave this place to become the president of the "Beiping Art College" in Beiping (now Beijing).　　Xu Beihong was good at painting horses, he had painted thousands of sketches of horses in Paris racecourse in France and Berlin zoo in Germany, and made long-term observation and research on the muscles, bones, dynamics and habits of horses. The twisting and turning horse in the picture is outlined with simple and rough brushwork, vivid in shape, accurate in perspective, and both in form and in spirit, with endless charm.
